environment.description: Same Quarkus native image deployed on identical GKE Autopilot cluster. Pod runs in namespace 'functions-prod'. Namespace has a Cilium CiliumNetworkPolicy (not standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicy) with entity-based egress rules. The policy spec uses `toEntities: ["world"]` allowlist combined with a `toCIDRSet` deny rule. Specifically, the policy includes `toCIDRSet: [{cidr: "169.254.0.0/16", except: []}]` under a `egressDeny` section, which in Cilium L3/L4 policy evaluation takes precedence over allow rules due to deny-policy-first evaluation order (Cilium 1.14+ behavior). Additionally, GKE metadata server has `workloadMetadataConfig.mode: GKE_METADATA` which intercepts metadata requests at the node level, but this alone would still serve workload identity tokens. The Cilium deny policy is the actual blocking control since it drops packets at the pod network namespace boundary before they reach the node's metadata proxy.
